findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the RDS database, including any sensitive employee/catalog data, is stored unencrypted on disk, violating encryption-at-rest requirements.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the MySQL database instance directly to the internet rather than restricting it to the private network.

The database password is sourced from var.password with no indication of use of a secrets manager, and the same variable is later embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, increasing risk of credential leakage.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database username and password (var.password) in cleartext inside a PHP config file written to disk, and user_data itself is visible via the EC2 metadata service to anyone with instance or API access, exposing plaintext credentials.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance role (assumable by any EC2 instance using this profile) full administrative control over S3, EC2, and RDS services, far exceeding least privilege for an application server.

Ingress on port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR block rather than being scoped to only the specific application security group/instances that require database access, unnecessarily widening the network attack surface within the VPC.
